title: 2026-11-05_Exaramel_Backdoor_Investigation_b39
description: Investigate a compromised system infected with the Exaramel backdoor, a component of the Sandworm malware family.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has been compromised by the Exaramel backdoor, a component of the Sandworm malware family. Exaramel is a backdoor written in Go language deployed in the Centreon directory. It ensures persistence via a scheduled task (Cron) and communicates with its command and control servers via HTTPS. Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Exaramel2023! Enter 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Exaramel2023! Enter 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all running and inactive services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or startup behavior.
4. Identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
The service responsible for the suspicious activity is Exaramel.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list all running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match typical system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to check for any unusual network listeners.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the target host using the provided credentials.
2. Inspect the suspicious service identified in the previous task using the command: `systemctl cat Exaramel.service`
3. Look for the port number specified in the ExecStart command.
4. Verify the port number by checking the network listeners using the command: `ss -tulnp`
The network port associated with this communication is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status Exaramel.service` to check the status and configuration of the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number in the ExecStart command within the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to confirm the port number is being used by the service.

levels.title: Identify System Information Collection
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all systemd services and timers using the commands: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` and `systemctl list-timers --all`
3. Look for any services or timers that are responsible for collecting system information.
4. Identify the service or timer responsible for this activity.
The service or timer responsible for this activity is local-inventory.timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers and their associated services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services or timers with names or descriptions that indicate they are collecting system information.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `journalctl -u <service>` to check the logs of the suspicious service.
